subject: Control Plane: Admin role scoping & SCIM cutover checklist
messages:
From: Susan Lewis <susan.lewis@brightwell.com>
To: logan.wright@redwood.ai, olga.petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: DevOps Team <devops@brightwell.com>
Date: 2026-08-16T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private control plane — identity cutover window and questions

Hi Logan / Olga,

Thanks again for the overview yesterday. We reviewed the admin role matrix and have a couple of asks before we confirm the maintenance window: 1) we need a clear mapping from our Okta groups to Redwood control-plane roles (Admin / Operator / ReadOnly) that preserves our audit trail, 2) we want to be sure SCIM provisioning will only create service accounts flagged as non-interactive, and 3) can you confirm how fallback looks if our SAML assertions are missing an attribute mid-cutover?

We're aiming for a mid-September maintenance window but will lock it only after the mapping and rollback plan are validated.

Attachments: saml-attribute-map-v1.pdf

Thanks,
Susan
Director of IT Operations
Brightwell Analytics
From: logan.wright@redwood.ai
To: Susan Lewis <susan.lewis@brightwell.com>
Cc: olga.petrov@redwood.ai, mina.haddad@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-16T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private control plane — identity cutover window and questions

Susan — thanks, this is helpful. High level answers up front: 1) we can implement an attribute-to-role mapping table and persist the original assertion for audit; 2) SCIM provisioning can tag service accounts as non-interactive and add a managed attribute so they are excluded from MFA policies; 3) fallback behaviour depends on the assertion — we support attribute defaults and a safe-mode where requests are routed to a hosted control plane account with limited privileges.

Detailed mapping draft and a short rollback sequence attached (see scim-delta-plan-v2.xlsx). I want to run through the proposed role scoping with security and then propose two candidate cutover windows (one weekend, one weekday-night).

Next steps: Olga and Mina will own the mapping review; Ben will run the SCIM acceptance tests. Can each of you confirm availability?

— Logan
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: olga.petrov@redwood.ai
To: logan.wright@redwood.ai, mina.haddad@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Cc: Susan Lewis <susan.lewis@brightwell.com>, DevOps Team <devops@brightwell.com>
Date: 2026-08-16T12:24:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private control plane — identity cutover window and questions

Thanks Logan. Quick operational clarifications from our side:

- Role scoping: we will publish an "admin-role-matrix.csv" that lists required Okta group names, assertion attributes, and exact Redwood role grants (namespace, read/write, operator). This file will be the source of truth during the cutover.
- SCIM provisioning: we will run SCIM in delta mode for two full days in staging to validate both creates and group deltas. Production will start with a dry-run (no writes) and then a single, coordinated write pass.
- Assertion gaps: default mapping policy will assign the least-privilege role (ReadOnly) when critical attributes are missing. If the customer's Okta drops an attribute for >5m, our routing rule will mark the session for manual review and route requests to the hosted fallback at reduced quota.

I have put questions inline in the shared Drive doc for Susan around group naming consistency. Also flagging that we need Okta Support looped for SAML metadata refresh coordination.

Olga
Product Security — Identity Integrations
Redwood Inference
From: mina.haddad@redwood.ai
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai, logan.wright@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Cc: Susan Lewis <susan.lewis@brightwell.com>
Date: 2026-08-17T08:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private control plane — identity cutover window and questions

Looping back with test plan specifics so we can sign off:

- Staging tests (owner: Mina): run 48hr SCIM delta ingestion, assertion replay for a 30-day window, and simulated attribute loss scenarios. Pass criteria: no unscoped grants, all writes reversible via delta-log.
- Acceptance tests (owner: Ben): end-to-end user provisioning (create, suspend, delete), service-account creation flagged as non-interactive, and policy enforcement checks (no MFA bypass).
- Cutover orchestration (owner: Logan): orchestration playbook that performs metadata swap, SCIM write-enable, and staged role promotion. Must include health-check probes and automatic rollback trigger if error rate >1% or if >2 critical users fail to authenticate.

I will schedule the staging run next week. Susan — can you confirm your team will provide a mirror subset of production groups for the staging run?

— Mina
Infrastructure Security Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Susan Lewis <susan.lewis@brightwell.com>
To: mina.haddad@redwood.ai, olga.petrov@redwood.ai, logan.wright@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-17T10:31:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private control plane — identity cutover window and questions

Thanks — yes, we can provide a sanitized mirror of groups and a subset of service accounts for staging. One operational ask: can you include an audit export at each stage (pre-write, post-write) so our compliance team can reconcile? Also we want DocuSign for the maintenance authorization.

We'll coordinate Okta Support for the SAML metadata push (they asked for a 48h lead).

— Susan
From: ben.carter@redwood.ai
To: Susan Lewis <susan.lewis@brightwell.com>, mina.haddad@redwood.ai, olga.petrov@redwood.ai, logan.wright@redwood.ai
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-19T15:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private control plane — identity cutover window and questions

Finalizing test schedule and pre-cutover checklist below — please review and confirm by EOD Friday:

Pre-cutover checklist (summary):
- SCIM staging delta run completed and logs archived (attachment: scim-delta-plan-v2.xlsx)
- Admin-role-matrix.csv reviewed and signed off by Brightwell security
- Audit exports scheduled at T-10m, T+10m and T+60m (Log retention: 90 days)
- Okta metadata push scheduled (Okta ticket: #78921)
- Canary: enable on 10% of operator traffic for 30 minutes, monitor 5s p95 auth latency and error spikes
- Fallback: automatic routing to hosted control plane if errors exceed threshold; manual rollback documented
- DocuSign maintenance approval link: https://redwood.docusign.com/MNT-4532

If no objections, we'll book the maintenance window for Sat 2026-09-12 02:00-05:00 UTC. Marissa — please raise the Change ID and update the runbook with the exact probe endpoints.

— Ben
Senior SRE, Identity Integrations
Redwood Inference
